reward_function_interface: def compute_reward(state, m_power, s_power, terminated) -> (reward, individual_reward_dict)
primary_objective: Land the lander on the landing pad at (0,0) as fast as possible with minimal fuel consumption.
state_space_summary: 8-dimensional vector: [x, y, vx, vy, angle, angular_velocity, leg1_contact, leg2_contact]
action_space_summary: Discrete: 0 (do nothing), 1 (fire left orientation engine), 2 (fire main engine), 3 (fire right orientation engine)

action_semantics.0: No engine thrust; coast or freefall.
action_semantics.1: Fire left orientation engine; applies torque to rotate lander clockwise and a small lateral force.
action_semantics.2: Fire main engine; applies upward thrust (opposite to lander's tip direction) to slow descent or ascend.
action_semantics.3: Fire right orientation engine; applies torque to rotate lander counter-clockwise and a small lateral force.

state_semantics.0: x-coordinate of lander center, normalized to [-1,1] relative to viewport width.
state_semantics.1: y-coordinate of lander center, normalized relative to viewport height; pad at ~0.
state_semantics.6: Boolean: left leg ground contact (1 if contact).
state_semantics.7: Boolean: right leg ground contact (1 if contact).

intended_behavior_phases: Phase 1: Stabilize and approach the landing pad from above.
Phase 2: Controlled descent with main engine braking to reduce vertical speed.
Phase 3: Final alignment and soft touchdown with both legs contacting the pad.

required_action_by_phase.Phase 1: Use orientation engines (actions 1 and 3) to correct horizontal drift and maintain upright orientation; occasional main engine (action 2) to control altitude.
required_action_by_phase.Phase 2: Main engine (action 2) primarily for braking; orientation engines as needed to keep lander upright and centered.
required_action_by_phase.Phase 3: Main engine (action 2) for soft landing; orientation engines for fine alignment; avoid unnecessary thrust to prevent overshoot.

necessary_behaviors: Maintain upright orientation (angle near 0) to ensure main engine thrust is vertical.
Use main engine to decelerate vertical velocity before touchdown.
Use orientation engines to correct horizontal velocity and position over the pad.
Achieve both legs in contact with ground simultaneously for stable landing.
success_signals_available_to_reward: Both legs ground contact (state[6]==1 and state[7]==1) while lander is near pad (x near 0, y near 0).
Low vertical and horizontal velocities at touchdown.
Low fuel consumption (m_power integrated over episode).
failure_or_stop_signals_available_to_rew: Crash: lander body contacts ground (game_over flag).
High impact velocity or large angle at ground contact.
dangerous_local_optima: Hovering indefinitely at high altitude without landing (avoids crash but never succeeds).
Landing far from pad (outside pad area) but with low velocity – satisfies soft landing but misses primary objective.
Using only orientation engines to drift sideways without main engine braking – may lead to crash or out-of-bounds.
Overusing main engine causing ascent away from pad – wastes fuel and time.
primary_selection_metric: Success rate (landing on pad with both legs contact and low velocity) within a fixed episode length.
proxy_metrics: Distance to pad (x, y) at each step.
diagnostic_metrics: Time spent with both legs in contact.
reward_design_constraints: Reward must be differentiable or decomposable into interpretable components.
Avoid large negative rewards for exploration; use mild penalties for fuel and large angle.
Provide positive reward for progress toward pad (e.g., decreasing distance) to guide sparse success.
Penalize crashes and out-of-bounds strongly to discourage unsafe behavior.
Do not penalize orientation engine usage excessively as it is necessary for stability.
Ensure reward scale is balanced so that main engine thrust reward does not dominate orientation rewards.
